Drives a hobby servo on a PWM-capable pin — To Angle for a positional servo (SG90-style, holds a 0-180° angle), Rotate for a continuous-rotation (360°) one (spins at a speed and direction), Release to cut the signal.

actions.description: Moves a positional servo to a fixed angle (0-180°) and holds it there.

configurations.description: Board pin the servo's signal wire is connected to.
Target angle, in degrees (0-180). Values outside the range are clamped.
Pulse width at 0°, in microseconds. Raise it if the servo strains at 0°.
Pulse width at 180°, in microseconds. Lower it if the servo strains at 180°.

outputSchema.name: angle
outputSchema.description: The clamped angle the servo was moved to, in degrees (0-180).

actions.description: Spins a continuous-rotation (360°) servo at the given speed and direction. Speed 0 stops it. The signal is held until the next action on the same pin.

configurations.description: Board pin the servo's signal wire is connected to.
Rotation speed, 0 (stopped) to 100 (max). Values outside the range are clamped.
Rotation direction.
Pulse width where this servo stands still, in microseconds. Nudge it (e.g. 1480 or 1520) if it creeps at Speed 0.
Microseconds from Stop Pulse to full speed.

outputSchema.name: speed
outputSchema.description: The clamped speed the servo was set to, 0-100.

actions.description: Cuts the signal: a positional servo stops holding its angle, a continuous one stops completely.

configurations.description: Board pin the servo's signal wire is connected to.

A PWM signal on a pin — for dimming a LED, setting a DC motor's speed (through a driver or transistor), driving a buzzer. Write sets a duty and holds it, Fade moves to one smoothly over a time, Stop cuts the signal. For servos, use the Servo component.

actions.description: Puts a PWM signal on the pin — Duty % of the time on — and holds it until the next action on the pin.

configurations.description: Board pin the signal goes out on — only PWM-capable pins are listed.
How much of the time the pin is on, from 0 (off) to 100 (fully on), in %. Decimals are fine (12.5). Bind it to follow a sensor.
Signal frequency, from 1 to 40000 Hz. 1000 suits LEDs; motors run quieter at 20000 (out of hearing); on a buzzer it's the note.
How Duty maps to the signal. Perceived brightness follows how the eye sees light, so a LED dims evenly (50% looks half as bright); keep Linear for motors and buzzers.
On for a load that's on when the pin is LOW — a LED wired from 3.3 V to the pin, an active-low driver. 100% is then fully on.
configurations.label: Active low

actions.description: Moves the pin's duty smoothly to To over Duration, then holds it — a LED fading in or out, a motor easing up.

configurations.description: Board pin the signal goes out on — only PWM-capable pins are listed.
The duty to end at, from 0 to 100, in %.
How long the fade takes, in milliseconds — 0 jumps straight to To, up to 600000 (10 minutes). The flow waits for it, like a Delay.
The duty to start at, from 0 to 100, in %. Leave it empty to start where the pin is now (what the last Write or Fade left it at — 0 if none).
Signal frequency, from 1 to 40000 Hz. 1000 suits LEDs; motors run quieter at 20000 (out of hearing); on a buzzer it's the note.
How Duty maps to the signal. Perceived brightness follows how the eye sees light, so a LED dims evenly (50% looks half as bright); keep Linear for motors and buzzers.
On for a load that's on when the pin is LOW — a LED wired from 3.3 V to the pin, an active-low driver. 100% is then fully on.
configurations.label: Active low

outputSchema.name: duty
outputSchema.description: The duty it ended at (To), in %.

actions.description: Cuts the signal and frees the pin.
